newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Jan 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Jan 10.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- WEN WEI PO -- Chinese President Jiang Zemin stressed the central government would not interfere with Hong Kong's internal affairs, and expressed hope that Hong Kong could play a special role after the handover.
-- The director of the Hong Kong and Macau Affairs Office, Lu Ping, said the Hong Kong provisional legislature could start passing laws before the handover.

-- SING TAO DAILY -- A provisional legislature member, Leung Chun-ying, said most government officials were waiting for Chief Executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa's measures to crack down on property market speculations.
-- MING PAO -- Chief Executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa and the Democratic Party agreed to meet every two months following their first meeting on Thursday.
-- Many women in Shanghai are earning more than their husbands, and demanding that their children should take their family names instead of their husbands'.
-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- China will next week launch its largest corporate bond issue, worth 3.5 billion yuan, to help finance railway projects.

-- The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's deputy chief executive said the slowdown in the Hong Kong economy and China's credit squeeze were behind a sharp increase in provisioning by local banks last year.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Airline analysts said China's "billion people syndrome" would make the listing of mainland airlines attractive, but added there was uncertainty over how much investors would pay for their potential.
